anomalies.observed: On the CM4 sheet, ComputeModule4-CM4 (Module2A) pin 99 (Global_EN) and pin 98 (Camera_GPIO) both carry the same net label NET0027, i.e. the camera GPIO pin is tied to the CM4 power‑enable net (the same net that also goes to the enable switch SW7 pin 2 and to buffer U29's output).
anomalies.expected: The specification states the GLOBAL_EN net is 'tied directly to SW1 pin 2' with no other members, and describes pin 99 as the Global_EN signal; Camera_GPIO (pin 98) is a separate GPIO that should not share the power‑enable net.

evidence.quote: CM4 sheet, Module2A left column bottom: pin 98 'Camera_GPIO' -> NET0027 and pin 99 'Global_EN' -> NET0027 (same label box)
Module1 pin 99 (Global_EN) — GLOBAL_EN net, tied directly to SW1 pin 2 ... the netlist confirms there is currently no delay/sequencing IC on this net, only a direct switch connection.

anomalies.impact: The CM4 power‑enable line is shorted to the camera GPIO. Whatever drives the enable net (the U29 buffer / SW7 switch) also drives the camera GPIO and vice‑versa; a camera‑side load or the e‑stop/LED logic that toggles NET0027 can pull Global_EN low and prevent the CM4 from booting, or conversely the enable logic can disturb the camera interface.

parsed.summary: Most of the board matches the documented reference design (16 MHz CAN crystals, LTC4412 + P‑MOS USB ideal‑diode, isolated CAN transceivers, SN74LVC1G07 e‑stop/LED buffers, WS2812 chain, ISL54222 analog switches). The one deviation I can read off the drawing is that CM4 pin 98 (Camera_GPIO) and pin 99 (Global_EN) are both labelled NET0027, merging the camera GPIO into the power‑enable net that the spec says contains only pin 99 and the enable switch.
